summary: OpenAI describes the engineering techniques behind GPT-5.6's efficiency gains, including inference-stack optimizations (load balancing, kernel rewrites, speculative decoding, KV-cache tuning) and agentic-harness design for context and prompt-cache management, many of which were executed autonomously by GPT-5.6 Sol itself.

mechanisms.reason: The document states concrete percentage reductions in serving cost and per-token efficiency from kernel, speculative-decoding and training optimizations.
mechanisms.quote: These efforts, combined with broader kernel advancements from GPT‑5.6 Sol, reduced end-to-end serving costs by 20%.

mechanisms.reason: The lab describes its own model autonomously executing substantial engineering work (kernel rewriting, training supervision) in place of human engineers, an instance of agent-executed work at scale.
mechanisms.quote: With Codex, GPT‑5.6 Sol autonomously rewrote and optimized our production kernels, the core code that executes the mathematical operations that make up the model.

practices.reason: Speculative decoding, kernel and KV-cache optimizations are described with stated gains but are tied to OpenAI's own infrastructure and proprietary Triton/Gluon tooling, so they inform rather than directly transfer to our stack.
practices.quote: The resulting improvements increased token-generation efficiency by more than 15%.

practices.reason: The append-only context and deterministic tool-ordering design for preserving cache prefixes is concrete enough to implement in our own agent harness and states a resulting benefit.
practices.quote: the harness treats all model-visible history as append-only: new messages, tool results, and environment updates are added at the end rather than inserted into earlier context.

practices.reason: The open-source FpSan tool for validating floating-point kernel correctness is a transferable verification method usable outside OpenAI.
practices.quote: We’ve also heavily invested in verification tooling, such as the open-source tool FpSan (Floating-Point Sanitizer), to help validate the correctness of the kernels written by GPT‑5.6 Sol.

practices.reason: GPT-5.6 Sol is reported to beat a rival model on a coding-agent benchmark at less than half the cost, and cheaper tiers match prior intelligence at reduced price, which changes model selection for coding and cost-sensitive workloads.
practices.quote: Our flagship model, GPT‑5.6 Sol, with max reasoning outperforms Claude Fable 5 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index at less than half of the cost.
